unit.why: Two separate short anecdotes about R. Levi Yitzhak of Berdichev, each cited from a different book: R. Barukh of Medzhybizh's mockery of him, and his sleepless night before taking the lulav.

stories.start_quote: שמענו בבירור שקה״ק רבי׳ ברוך נ״ע ממעזבוז
stories.summary_en: R. Barukh of Medzhybizh used to mock R. Levi Yitzhak of Berdichev; after Levi Yitzhak's death he explained that he did it to protect him, because the heavenly seraphim envied his great love and awe of God.

quotes: הי׳ דרכו לצחוק ולהלעיג מאוד מהגה״ק ר׳ לוי יצחק
tags.why: One tzaddik habitually mocks another; the hostility turns out to be only apparent.

quotes: ואחר פטירתו אמר שעשה זה מפני
tags.why: The true reason for the mockery is revealed only after Levi Yitzhak's death.
The mockery was meant to sweeten judgment and shield him from heavenly envy.
Levi Yitzhak's awe of God is the cause of the heavenly envy.
The tale is told under the heading of Levi Yitzhak's greatness.
A tzaddik's deliberate ridicule of another.

stories.start_quote: בעת שהי׳ מגיע למצות לולב ואתרוג
stories.summary_en: Before the commandment of lulav and etrog, Levi Yitzhak of Berdichev stayed awake all night, roaring like a lion, dancing and rejoicing in longing for the moment he would take them and say the blessing.

tags.why: The scene is the night before the lulav commandment on Sukkot.

quotes: היה נעור כל הלילה ושאג כארי
tags.why: Burning fervor: roaring and staying up all night.
The tale illustrates his love of the commandments.
